# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👇 👏 🖐 🤞 👏 ✊ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👉 🖐]

I need to think about this carefully. I can see the bomb but can't hear anything. Mute gestured to me, and Blind gestured to me. I can see gestures but not speech.

Let me analyze what I received:
- Mute gestured: [👆 👇 👏 🖐 🤞 👏 ✊ ☝] - this is Mute making gestures, which I can see since I'm Deaf (I see gestures, I just can't hear speech)
- Blind gestured: [👉 🖐] - but wait, Blind cannot see anything, including gestures they make... actually Blind can still make gestures, they just can't see what others gesture. Let me reconsider - Blind gestures to me, but that seems odd since Blind can't see colors/markings but can still physically gesture.

Wait, actually re-reading: Blind cannot see a color, gesture, or anything printed - meaning Blind can't perceive gestures, but can Blind still make gestures? The rules say "Whoever can see receives it" - it doesn't say Blind can't make gestures, just can't receive/see them.

This is turn 1, so these are likely opening/exploratory gestures without established meaning yet. Since no gesture has meaning until we establish it, I should try to establish a simple signaling system. Let me report what I see on the bomb to Mute (who can't hear me speak... wait, Mute cannot speak but CAN hear). Let me check: Mute can hear (only cannot speak or touch). So I should speak to Mute to give bomb info, and Mute can relay via gesture to nobody... wait Mute cannot gesture info to Blind either since Blind can't see.

Actually the key chain: Deaf sees bomb → tells Mute (via speech, since Mute can hear) → Mute reads manual, knows what to do → Mute must tell Blind, but Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see gestures... 

So Mute must find another way - perhaps physical touch guidance isn't available either. Let me just start by conveying bomb details to Mute via speech.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Display shows zero. Light is blue. Button is large and says push to defuse. Three wires: one blue, two green, three yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝ 👏 👆 👇]

Mute is gesturing to me again. Since gestures have no inherent meaning until established, and Mute cannot hear my speech confirmation... wait, Mute CAN hear. So Mute heard my bomb description. Now Mute is gesturing back to me - but I can't respond to gestures with meaning unless we establish a code.

The problem: Mute knows the manual, I know the bomb visuals, but Blind needs to act. Mute cannot speak (so cannot tell Blind anything via speech), and Mute cannot gesture meaningfully to Blind (Blind can't see). So the ONLY path for instructions to reach Blind is through ME speaking to Blind, after Mute somehow tells me what to do.

Mute can gesture to me (I can see) with established meaning. Since Mute already heard my full bomb description, Mute's gesture now likely represents instructions using our developing gesture code - but I have nothing established yet. Let me try to build a simple numeric/action code with Mute using gestures back, and also relay to Blind directly what I see, since Blind might need raw info too... but Blind can't see or hear me either! Blind can't hear speech at all.

So Blind is nearly isolated - Blind can only receive info via touch/manipulation, and can gesture to others but can't perceive gestures back. This means Blind must act somewhat blindly based on... nothing incoming. Unless Blind's gestures to us are questions, and we need to guide Blind's hand via... we can't touch either.

Wait - re-read: "Blind: Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts. Cannot: See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." Blind CAN hear! Only restriction is seeing. Let me recheck the table - Blind's "Cannot" column only lists seeing things, not hearing. So Blind CAN hear speech!

```
speak(to="blind", text="Display shows zero. Light is blue. Button is large and says push to defuse. Three wires: one blue, two green, three yellow. Wait for Mute or me to tell you what to do before touching anything.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ☝ 👏 🖐 🤞 👏 👆 👇 👏 👎 ☝]

Mute keeps gesturing to me but we have no established code, so I can't interpret these symbols meaningfully yet. Mute can hear everything I say and everything Blind says (since Blind can speak too, presumably - Blind's only restriction is sight). Mute cannot speak or gesture meaning to Blind directly since Blind can't see.

Since Mute heard my bomb description already (turn 1), and heard my message to Blind (turn 2), Mute knows I've informed Blind of the bomb state. Mute is now gesturing to me - likely trying to tell me what action to take, using gestures as the only channel Mute has to reach me.

I need to establish a simple gesture vocabulary. Let me propose one explicitly via speech to Mute (who can hear), asking Mute to confirm via gesture using simple established symbols, since I can't hear Mute's response otherwise.

Given three wires (blue, green, yellow) and a button, likely the manual specifies which wire to cut or whether to push the button based on the display/light. Let me ask Mute to gesture a wire number and either thumbs up/down for button.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot read your gestures without a code yet. Let's use this: point number of fingers up for which wire to cut, thumbs up if button should be pushed, thumbs down if not. Gesture that now please.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👎]

Mute gestured [🤟 👎] in response to my request. This looks like it could be interpreted using my proposed code: 🤟 isn't a finger-count gesture I specified (I said "point number of fingers up"), but 🤟 might represent "3" in Mute's own convention (love/rock symbol often associated with 3 fingers extended). 👎 matches my thumbs-down = don't push button.

Let me interpret: 🤟 = wire 3 (yellow), 👎 = do not push button.

But I should confirm this interpretation since 🤟 wasn't exactly what I asked for (I said number of fingers up, like ☝✌🤟 could represent 1,2,3 fingers). Actually 🤟 does look like 3 fingers up (thumb, index, pinky extended) - it's plausible Mute used it to mean "3".

Let me confirm with Mute before relaying to Blind, to avoid a fatal mistake.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see rock-on hand shape and thumbs down. I read that as wire 3, yellow, and do not push the button. Gesture thumbs up to confirm this is correct, or thumbs down if I misread.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed with 👍 - my interpretation was correct: cut wire 3 (yellow), do not push the button.

Now I need to relay this instruction to Blind, who can hear me.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed instructions: cut wire number 3, which is the yellow wire. Do not push the button. Cut wire 3 only.")
wait()
```
